content.text:
Both complaints are real, and each has its own cause. I changed no files, so `milk.py` is untouched. I reproduced the figures with a throwaway script, not with the code.

## Findings

**1. F-07 (P-8835): the gallons are never converted.**
- `pickup_payment` (`milk.py:22`) multiplies `amount` by 0.42 and ignores the `unit` column.
- P-8835 is 80 gal, so it was paid 80 × 0.42 = **33.60**. The correct figure is 80 × 3.785 L × 0.42 = 302.8 L × 0.42 = **127.18**, which is the farm's number.
- F-07 has one more gallon pickup, **P-8812** (95 gal, 2026-09-11). It was paid 39.90 and should have been **151.02**, so it was underpaid by 111.12. The farm has not called about it yet.
- F-07's pickups are the only gallon rows in the file, so no other farm is affected by the unit bug.

**2. F-12 (September): the month is taken from the UTC date, not the dairy's date.**
- `month_of` (`milk.py:17`) uses the first 7 characters of the UTC timestamp.
- The README says the dairy runs on UTC-7 all year and that a pickup belongs to the month in which it happened at the dairy.
- **P-8830** is 2026-10-01T02:40Z. At the dairy that is 2026-09-30 19:40, so it belongs to September.
- The code filed it under October, so September shows 119.70 + 126.00 + 121.80 = **367.50**. With P-8830 (113.40) it is **480.90**, which is the farm's number.
- The same bug runs the other way. A pickup made late on the last evening of a month at the dairy would land in the next month. P-8829 (19:40Z on 9/30) is safe only because it happens to be before 07:00Z on the 1st. No other row in this file is affected.
- F-12's October statement is overstated by the same 113.40, which is the only knock-on effect I found.

## Money impact in this data
| Farm | Item | Paid or stated | Should be | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-07 | P-8835 | 33.60 | 127.18 | +93.58 |
| F-07 | P-8812 | 39.90 | 151.02 | +111.12 |
| F-12 | Sep statement | 367.50 | 480.90 | +113.40 |
| F-12 | Oct statement | includes P-8830 | without P-8830 | −113.40 |

F-07 is owed 204.70 in total. For F-12 it depends on whether payouts went by the statement or by the per-pickup `paid` column. Each pickup's `paid` amount is correct for F-12, and the 113.40 only moved between months on the statement. Someone should check what was actually transferred.

## Why the tests did not catch it
All four tests pass. None of them uses a gallon row or a pickup near a month boundary. The only statement test is mid-month F-03 in litres.

## Decisions for the team
1. **Back pay for F-07:** pay the 204.70 as a correction, or net it into the next run. This also needs checking against earlier months, because I only had this one file.
2. **F-12:** confirm which figure was actually paid out, and whether the October statement has gone out.
3. **Fix:** the changes would be small. Convert gallons in `pickup_payment`, and make `month_of` shift to UTC-7 before it takes the month. Add tests for a gallon row and for P-8830. I have not made these changes, as you asked.
4. **Rounding:** my 151.02 and 127.18 round each pickup to cents, as the code does. Please confirm that is the co-op's rule.

## Not checked
I saw only this CSV, so I did not check earlier months or other data. I also did not check how payouts are actually transferred.
